karty.priklad: Dw i'n gweithio yn yr Adran Farchnata.
karty.priklad_cs: I work in the Marketing Department (marchnata → [f]archnata after the feminine adran).
karty.mnemo: Our department RAN an AD (AD-RAN) in huge red neon letters.

karty.priklad: Rhoddodd hi'r nodyn yn yr amlen.
karty.priklad_cs: She put the note in the envelope.
karty.mnemo: I AM LENding (AM-LEN) you an envelope, sealed with red wax.

extra.pozn: after ei = her: ei hamlen hi; related: llythyr = letter

karty.priklad: Diolch am dy gefnogaeth di.
karty.priklad_cs: Thanks for your support (cefnogaeth → [g]efnogaeth after dy).
karty.mnemo: cefn = back: support means having someone's back – holding a red shield behind them.

karty.priklad: Roedd y gynulleidfa wrth ei bodd.
karty.priklad_cs: The audience was delighted (cynulleidfa → [g]ynulleidfa after y, feminine; wrth ei bodd: ei = 'her', because cynulleidfa is feminine).
karty.mnemo: cynnull = to gather (as in cynulliad, assembly) + -fa (place): the people gathered in one place – an audience fanning themselves in a red-hot theatre.

karty.priklad: Gwasanaeth yn yr eglwys gadeiriol!
karty.priklad_cs: A service in the cathedral! (gadeiriol is always mutated in this fixed phrase: cadeiriol → [g]adeiriol after the feminine eglwys)
karty.mnemo: cadair = chair, throne: the church with the bishop's throne – and blazing red stained glass.

karty.priklad: Gwela i ti wrth y fynedfa am saith.
karty.priklad_cs: I'll see you by the entrance at seven (mynedfa → [f]ynedfa after y, feminine).
karty.mnemo: mynd (to go) + -fa (place): an entrance lit by flaming torches.

karty.priklad: Aethon ni i'r brotest yng Nghaerdydd.
karty.priklad_cs: We went to the protest in Cardiff (protest → [b]rotest after y, feminine).
karty.mnemo: Same as English: protestors marching behind a burning red flare.

karty.priklad: Dw i'n mynd i'r siop trin gwallt bore fory.
karty.priklad_cs: I'm going to the hairdresser's tomorrow morning.
karty.mnemo: trin = to treat, gwallt = hair: the shop with the red-and-white pole where they treat your hair.

karty.priklad: Mae Cymru'n dibynnu ar dwristiaeth.
karty.priklad_cs: Wales depends on tourism (twristiaeth → [d]wristiaeth after ar).
karty.mnemo: twrist (tourist) + -iaeth: tourism – sunburnt tourists packed onto the beach.

karty.priklad: Dw i'n meddwl bod yr amgylchedd yn bwysig iawn.
karty.priklad_cs: I think the environment is very important (pwysig → [b]wysig after yn).
karty.mnemo: am (around) + cylch (circle): everything around us – protect it, or the polar ice caps melt.

karty.cs_upresneni: a memory of something, not memory as an ability
karty.priklad: Oes atgof arbennig gyda chi o gyngerdd?
karty.priklad_cs: Have you got a special memory of a concert? (cyngerdd → [g]yngerdd after o)
karty.mnemo: at + cof (memory): a memory floats up like an ice floe.

sever.priklad: Oes gynnoch chi atgof arbennig o gyngerdd?
sever.priklad_cs: Have you got a special memory of a concert?
sever.pozn: north: gynnoch chi instead of gyda chi (L6)

karty.priklad: Wnei di edrych dros y cofnodion yma? – Edrycha i drostyn nhw ar ôl cinio.
karty.priklad_cs: Will you look over these minutes? – I'll look over them after lunch.
karty.mnemo: cof (memory) + nod (mark): a mark to help the memory – minutes scratched into the snow.

karty.cs_upresneni: a more literary word than ffrind
karty.priklad: Mae Dafydd yn hen gyfaill i fi.
karty.priklad_cs: Dafydd is an old friend of mine (cyfaill → [g]yfaill after hen).
karty.mnemo: An old friend: a CAVALIER (CYF-AILL) in an ice-blue cloak.

sever.priklad: Mae Dafydd yn hen gyfaill i mi.
sever.priklad_cs: Dafydd is an old friend of mine (cyfaill → [g]yfaill after hen).
sever.pozn: north: i mi instead of i fi (not in the coursebook)

karty.priklad: Mae fy chwaer i'n gyfrifydd.
karty.priklad_cs: My sister is an accountant (cyfrifydd → [g]yfrifydd after yn).
karty.mnemo: cyfrif (to count) + -ydd (person): the accountant spends all day counting penguins.

karty.priklad: Beth yw cysylltiad Catrin Zara ag Abercastell?
karty.priklad_cs: What's Catrin Zara's connection with Abercastell?
karty.mnemo: cysylltu = to connect: a blue cable laid under the Arctic ice connects the two.

sever.priklad: Be ydy cysylltiad Catrin Zara ag Abercastell?
sever.priklad_cs: What's Catrin Zara's connection with Abercastell?
sever.pozn: north: Be ydy instead of Beth yw (L5)

karty.priklad: Es i â'r presgripsiwn at y fferyllydd.
karty.priklad_cs: I took the prescription to the chemist.
karty.mnemo: The chemist takes the FERRY (FFER-yll-ydd) across to deliver ice packs to the island.

karty.priklad: Pa mor aml wyt ti'n defnyddio ffigurau?
karty.priklad_cs: How often do you use figures?
karty.mnemo: Same as English: figures frozen on a blue digital display.

extra.pozn: a question, so wyt ti (not rwyt ti) is right

karty.priklad: Dw i yn poeni am fy ffitrwydd i.
karty.priklad_cs: I really do worry about my fitness.
karty.mnemo: ffit + -rwydd = fitness: training laps round a freezing ice rink.

karty.priklad: Mae'r plant yn cael edrych ar eu gliniaduron nhw ar ôl swper.
karty.priklad_cs: The children are allowed to look at their laptops after supper.
karty.mnemo: glin (knee, lap) + -iadur as in cyfrifiadur (computer): a lap computer with a cold blue glow.

sever.priklad: Mae'r plant yn cael sbio ar eu gliniaduron nhw ar ôl swper.
sever.priklad_cs: The children are allowed to look at their laptops after supper.

karty.priklad: Oes diddordeb gyda ti yn y cwrs gramadeg?
karty.priklad_cs: Are you interested in the grammar course?
karty.mnemo: GRAMMAR (GRAMA-deg): the rules carved into a block of ice.

sever.priklad: Oes gen ti ddiddordeb yn y cwrs gramadeg?
sever.priklad_cs: Are you interested in the grammar course?
sever.pozn: north: gen ti instead of gyda ti (L6), soft mutation after gen: diddordeb → [dd]iddordeb

karty.priklad: Dw i'n siarad Cymraeg yn y gweithle bob dydd.
karty.priklad_cs: I speak Welsh in the workplace every day.
karty.mnemo: gwaith (work) + lle (place): a workplace in an ice-cold warehouse.

karty.priklad: Rhaid i fi ysgrifennu nodyn ati hi.
karty.priklad_cs: I must write her a note.
karty.mnemo: A snowman NODs (NOD-yn) and hands you a note.

sever.priklad: Rhaid i mi sgwennu nodyn ati hi.
sever.priklad_cs: I must write her a note.
sever.pozn: north: i mi instead of i fi, sgwennu instead of ysgrifennu (both not in the coursebook)

karty.priklad: Mwynheuon ni berfformiad y gerddorfa.
karty.priklad_cs: We enjoyed the orchestra's performance (perfformiad → [b]erfformiad as the object; cerddorfa → [g]erddorfa after y, feminine).
karty.mnemo: Same as English: a performance on ice skates.

karty.priklad: Ces i bigiad gan y nyrs ddoe.
karty.priklad_cs: The nurse gave me an injection yesterday (pigiad → [b]igiad as the object).
karty.mnemo: A PIGgy (PIG-iad) needs an injection – and the needle is ice-cold.

sever.priklad: Ges i bigiad gan y nyrs ddoe.
sever.priklad_cs: The nurse gave me an injection yesterday (pigiad → [b]igiad as the object).
sever.pozn: north: ges i instead of ces i (not in the coursebook)

karty.priklad: Rhoddodd y meddyg bresgripsiwn i fi.
karty.priklad_cs: The doctor gave me a prescription (presgripsiwn → [b]resgripsiwn as the object).
karty.mnemo: Same as English: the chemist hands your prescription over from a freezer.

sever.priklad: Rhoddodd y meddyg bresgripsiwn i mi.
sever.priklad_cs: The doctor gave me a prescription (presgripsiwn → [b]resgripsiwn as the object).
sever.pozn: north: i mi instead of i fi (not in the coursebook)

karty.priklad: Ga i fenthyg dy siswrn di?
karty.priklad_cs: Can I borrow your scissors? (benthyg → [f]enthyg after ga i)
karty.mnemo: SCISSORS (SISWRN) snipping snowflakes out of blue paper.

extra.pozn: singular in Welsh = one pair of scissors

karty.priklad: Wnei di edrych dros y traethawd yma? – Edrycha i drosto fe ar ôl cael paned.
karty.priklad_cs: Will you look over this essay? – I'll look over it after a cuppa.
karty.mnemo: Think of traeth (beach): an essay about the beach, written in winter while the sand is white with frost.

sever.priklad: Wnei di edrych dros y traethawd yma? – Edrycha i drosto fo ar ôl cael paned.
sever.priklad_cs: Will you look over this essay? – I'll look over it after a cuppa.
